name: Bear Trap / Ham Sandwich
keyCorrections: If they pull their leg free, your trap was too shallow, re-enter the trap deeper in your knee pit.
If you can't finish, your shin angle is wrong, turn your shin so the bone edge presses into their calf.
If they spin out, you lost upper body control, re-establish your grip on their collar or arm.
description: Use the bear trap (also called ham sandwich) to create a compression lock - Calf Slicer, from half butterfly or Half Guard, forcing the opponent to tap, expose their back, or give up the sweep.
shortInstruction: Trap their leg in your knee pit, drive your shin into their calf, compress, the bear trap is a Calf Slicer hidden in the Half Guard.
summary: The bear trap (ham sandwich) is a compression submission (Calf Slicer) that uses your shin bone against their calf muscle, with their leg trapped in the crook of your knee. It is most commonly entered from half butterfly or Half Guard when the opponent drives forward. The crushing pressure on their calf forces them to either tap, roll onto their back (giving you the sweep), or expose their back for a Back Take.
whyItWorks: The compression of the shin bone against the calf muscle creates intense pain and joint pressure, most opponents will tap or roll.
It works as a dilemma: tap from the Calf Slicer or give up the sweep/Back Take.
It can be entered without complex setup, if you have half butterfly and they drive forward, the bear trap is often available.
Danaher principle: compression locks are high-percentage because they work on a single joint (knee) with predictable anatomy.
commonMistakes: Letting their leg slide out of your knee pit, a shallow trap loses the compression.
Using your hands to pull their leg instead of your knee pit, the leg trap must be passive.
Forgetting to control their upper body, they will spin out of the bear trap.
Applying the Calf Slicer too aggressively, compression injuries can happen quickly.
coachingCues: Trap deep in the knee pit, drive with the shin.
Control the upper body, the bear trap is just the hook.
If they roll, follow to the sweep or Back Take.
Compression works, don't crank, just squeeze.
safetySummary: Calf Slicers apply intense pressure to the knee and calf, apply slowly and release on tap.
Do not apply the Calf Slicer explosively, the knee can be injured before the opponent feels the pain.
Not recommended for beginners, compression locks require experience to apply safely.

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Half butterfly or Half Guard: opponent drives forward → trap their leg in your knee pit (bear trap) → compress with shin → finish or sweep.

decisionTree.action: They tap → Calf Slicer finish. Reaction 2: They roll → sweep to top or Back Take.
The bear trap chains into the Back Take when they roll to escape the calf pressure.

moneyDetails: Trap their leg as deep as possible in your knee pit, the knee pit should be at or behind their knee joint.
Drive your shin bone (the sharp edge) into their calf muscle, the bone-on-muscle compression is the finish.
Control their upper body with an underhook or collar tie to prevent them from spinning away.
If they try to roll out of the Calf Slicer, release the compression and follow their roll, take the back or sweep.
nextStep: After the bear trap, learn the half butterfly to leg entanglement transitions.
fixItFast: Leg keeps sliding out? Trap it deeper in your knee pit, closer to your hip.
Compression not working? Adjust your shin angle, the bone edge, not the flat of the shin.
They roll away? Release the trap, follow their hips, take the back.
